pr_title: drivers: ethernet: enc424j600: Fix interrupt handling
pr_body:
This fixes an issue with interrupts being triggered before the
enc424j600 driver is ready to receive them or has configured the
interrupt sources which would prevent the driver from loading. An
optional Kconfig option has been added to allow not re-enabling
interrupts after an unknown interrupt has occured, this brings the
driver in-line with all other Zephyr ethernet drivers and the Linux
kernel encx24j600 driver.

Signed-off-by: Jamie McCrae <jamie.mccrae@lairdconnect.com>

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/35091

> I have an old olimax enc624j600 board which I attached to our BL5340 development board to use instead of the on-board enc424j600 to exclude any possible issues with the components on our board, this made no difference and I get the unknown interrupt error whilst at the same time someone else remove all the intermediatory components on our development board between the BL5340 and enc424j600 e.g. for level shifting which also made no difference. I then tested with an nRF5340-DK and the olimax enc624j600 and I see the exact same issue with the original code - it does not work:

I tested today: link board ETH with nRF52840DK, link board ETH with frdm_k64f, mikroETH100 with nRF52840. I can not reproduce issue that you describe. On BL5340, can you please connect AD0..AD14 and PSPCFG0 pins to GND and retest?
We have tested changing our interrupt pull-up resistor from 100K to 10K as per your board and grounded all AD pins (PSP was already grounded) and it has made no difference.
Are there different versions of enc424j600 which could explain the difference you are seeing?

> Are there different versions of enc424j600 which could explain the difference you are seeing?

Microchip's errata document seems to indicate only 1 silicon revision: A2

After further debugging it seems that the unknown interrupt was caused by the interrupt being triggered prior to the driver configuring the interrupt sources it wanted to receive, disabling interrupts until they have been configured has resolved the issue. Additionally given that no other network driver in zephyr nor the encx24j600 driver in the linux kernel operates in the way that this driver did operate in and given that it doesn't make any sense for a production IoT firmware (whereby if an unknown interrupt was received then this driver would essentially kill itself with no warnings by not re-enabling interrupts) I have moved the option to do that to be behind a Kconfig option which is opt-in
Closing this as we merged a different PR solution to the issue.

comments: I can not reproduce it with link_board_eth shield connected to nrf5340dk_nrf5340. Please check interrupt (INT) line, level shifter, pullups on your board.
It could also be related to errata number 4 as per https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/80477A.pdf

A logic trace of the interrupt line:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40387179/117967353-d80b2f80-b31c-11eb-866b-3b3741eb0b7a.png)
The first is the expected one and the second one what triggers the 'unknown interrupt', indeed the ESTAT register does show that an interrupt is not pending, so this could also be handled by only checking the interrupt source if the bit in ESTAT is set and if not, it continues on and re-enables the interrupt, or reads ESTAT first and doesn't disable the interrupt at all if that bit is not set since there is no interrupt to handle.

In fact that might even work better, moving the ESTAT read first and then only running the rest of the code if the MSB is set gets rid of the second blip altogether:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40387179/117968098-ba8a9580-b31d-11eb-9aa3-f66c8fbf2ea3.png)
I can change the fix to do that instead if preferred, thoughts?

Only two interrupt source are enabled [PHYLNK and PKTCNT](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/drivers/ethernet/eth_enc424j600.c#L719-L720). "the INT pin is driven low and the INT flag (ESTAT<15>) becomes set" only for these interrupt sources, not for any others. [continue at L:487](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/drivers/ethernet/eth_enc424j600.c#L487) is intentional to detect errors like spurious interrupts.

> There are 3 bits for interrupts that are not implemented as per the datasheet http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/devicedoc/39935b.pdf page 120 in the high byte (2 bits in the lower byte too), the lower 3 bits are reserved, that is "Ignore on read, don’t care on write", in the chip I have here, they are being returned as set hence the following error "[00:00:00.259,124] ethdrv: Unknown Interrupt, EIR: 0x0700"

It is not relevant because these interrupt sources are not enabled by the driver, and thus will not generate interrupt.

> The code in the driver works by waiting for an interrupt, then in a thread it waits for a semaphore and once received, disables interrupts on the enc424j600, it reads and then handles the interrupt and re-enables interrupts except in the case of it being an invalid interrupt, in which case it leaves interrupts disabled. This is not valid operation.

It is valid, I intentionally designed it that way, see above.

> So the issue may be that you have a different silicon revision of the enc424j600 chip or for any other number of reasons, however, the bug is with the driver code.

Well that can be, surely you have checked your hardware and signal integrity, then it must be the driver.

> The first is the expected one and the second one what triggers the 'unknown interrupt', indeed the ESTAT register does show that an interrupt is not pending,....

Maybe it is not the driver?

I enclose a zip with 2 traces and 2 outputs, one from before the changes and one from after. Logic traces can be viewed with saleae's viewer available from https://support.saleae.com/logic-software channel 0 is SPI clock, channel 1 is SPI MOSI, channel 2 is SPI MISO and channel 3 is the interrupt. You can use the saleae logic SPI decoder to view the SPI traffic from a glance.
[eth_checks.zip](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/6466896/eth_checks.zip)

For the record: I was able to reproduce it on nRF5340DK by changing used SPI node to spi2 (the same used on BL5340 board).  I can also confirm that clearing INTIE flag in EIE register right after reset (SETETHRST) fixes the issue.
Since I do not agree with the proposed changes in #35092, I have opened alternative #35439.

review_comments: NACK, this is intended as explained [here]( https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/35091#issuecomment-839813047)

This should be behind a Kconfig option that is disabled by default. A driver should not screw itself up because it received an event that it can safely ignore. Query: should an AT modem completely shut down if it receives a wrong command or emit an error and continue working as normal? This is useful for driver development and debugging but is nothing but extremely unhelpful in a production-grade firmware for an IoT device
No, it must not be ignored. To be clear, alternative to continue is k_oops()
This is not in-line with any other ethernet driver in zephyr nor the encx24j600 driver in the linux kernel, it is staying to keep all these drivers operating in the same expected way.
It is nonsense. Do not change it, do not introduce new config option. And please do not resolve unresolved conversation.
How this change is relevant to the bug?

Actually it is simpler to change 
```
enc424j600_set_sfru(dev, ENC424J600_SFR3_EIEL,
      			    ENC424J600_EIE_PKTIE | ENC424J600_EIE_LINKIE);
```

to 
```
enc424j600_write_sfru(dev, ENC424J600_SFR3_EIEL,
      			    ENC424J600_EIE_PKTIE | ENC424J600_EIE_LINKIE);
```

and place it in this line. This is what I wrote in the email as an example, all this is a bit too exhausting, I will open an alternative PR.
How this change is relevant to the bug?

Probably because of the code under it sets the sfru:
```
		enc424j600_set_sfru(context->dev, ENC424J600_SFR3_EIEL,
				    ENC424J600_EIE_INTIE);
```
And by skipping this is gets into a state whereby it does not handle other interrupts. With the continue there I can't get it working at all, with the continue gone it works every time without issue.
This explanation makes sense to me, but it should be in the commit message. (Description of how it behaved incorrectly before and how it'll behave correctly after this change.)
